Cross-model context (research launched; NO janitor revisions from it - context only, per maintainer). Motivation: the OSS-practice survey found cross-model critique is the one decorrelation mechanism with clean empirical support - Greptile's Model Inversion measured a model reviewing same-model-authored code at 53.7% recall vs 62.0% on another model's code, because 'the types of bugs a model introduces most often are the same types it's more likely to miss during review'; Goel et al. arXiv:2502.04313 report mistakes growing MORE similar as capability rises, and that LLM-judge scores favour models similar to the judge. Our current config is single-family: DEFAULT_MODEL claude-opus-4-8 (frontier), VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL claude-sonnet-4-6 (standard), DEFAULT_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6. Provider is inferred from the model name through pydantic-ai, so a non-Anthropic provider is already architecturally supported - this would be configuration, not new plumbing. Hard constraints on any candidate: Bedrock inference-profile id (plain on-demand ids raise ValidationException), and RELIABLE schema-constrained structured output, since every rebar LLM operation forces JSON-Schema output through pydantic-ai. Key framing recorded for whoever revisits: the goal is decorrelation, not replacement, so a slightly weaker model that fails DIFFERENTLY can be worth more as a reviewer than a stronger model that fails the same way.

## Design decision recorded: lazy-import + optional extra (NOT vendoring)
The plan review BLOCKed on two architectural findings (previous comment): the transitive `mistune` dependency, and `src/rebar/_vendor/` not being importable from the reconciler subprocess. Operator decision is **option 2**:

- `markdown_to_adf` / `adf_to_markdown` / `fit_markdown_to_adf_limit` **lazy-import marklas inside the function bodies**, and route `ImportError` to the existing plain-text `adf.py` fallback.
- marklas + mistune ship as a **pinned OPTIONAL extra**, not as vendored source. No `src/rebar/_vendor/` tree is created.

Reasoning:
1. It is the only option that preserves the documented stdlib-only engine contract (`pyproject.toml:69` — engine assets are stdlib-only package data; core `dependencies` stay pyyaml/jsonschema/referencing).
2. It mirrors three established degradation precedents in this repo — `agents`, `metrics`, `grounding` — all of which are optional extras behind lazy imports with a defined behaviour when absent.
3. It puts the "must tolerate a no-extras install" requirement exactly where it belongs: on `disparaged-parodistic-shrew` (3388)'s cutover, which has to handle the plain-`adf` path regardless. That requirement is being added to 3388 explicitly so it cannot be missed.

Option 1 (vendor marklas + mistune, ~398 KB / 56 files, under an engine-shipped path) was NOT chosen because it redefines a documented contract. It remains available to the operator later if the optional extra proves awkward in practice; this note is the deviation record. The epic's plan text, which pins `src/rebar/_vendor/marklas/`, is being updated with the same deviation + reasoning.

EXPERIMENT 2 — Gerrit webhook->diff gap (d251 S4a/S4b). Ran a REAL read-only experiment against the live public Gerrit gerrit-review.googlesource.com (no docker needed). PROVEN:
(a) Change-metadata JSON (GET /changes/?q=...&o=CURRENT_REVISION) is XSSI-guarded with the )]}' prefix and carries NO diff/patch field (HAS_DIFF_FIELD: False) — the webhooks-plugin payload is an EVENT (patchset-created metadata), strictly less than this, so the diff is NEVER in the webhook body.
(b) GET /changes/{n}/revisions/current/patch returns a BASE64 blob (first chars 'RnJvbSBi...'), which base64-decodes to a git format-patch ('From <sha> Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001 / Subject: [PATCH] ...'). So the receiver MUST make a separate authenticated REST call to obtain the diff; it must base64-decode the result.
(c) GET /changes/{n}/revisions/current/files/ returns JSON (XSSI-guarded) — the structured per-file alternative.
IMPLICATION: d251 S4b (918c) already has Round-9 AC ('fetches diff via Gerrit REST as diff_text=') and Round-10 AC ('invokes review_code() with a valid repo context / fetched checkout at the change ref'). The GAP the review caught is that the EPIC body's Round-9 seam still types the adapter as code_review_decision(diff_text)->{decision} (diff_text ONLY), contradicting S4b's Round-10 reality (needs diff_text + repo_root + ref). REMEDY: reconcile the epic seam contract to code_review_decision(diff_text, repo_root, ref)->{decision: PASS|BLOCK}, give it a concrete name+module, co-locate the error/fallback rule with the schema, and add an explicit covering AC; b744-WS6 (4119) must implement the SAME signature. Also: provision the bot's OUTBOUND read credential (Gerrit HTTP token works for REST /a/ AND git-over-HTTPS clone of the change ref) in S1 SSM scaffolding + S4a.
